title: Species of the same continent or sea are related despite differing stations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Species of the same continent or sea are related despite differing stations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The inhabitants of the same continent or sea show a pervasive affinity to one another, so that distinct but related species replace one another from place to place and across different habitats, rather than being replaced by forms from other continents living under similar conditions.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: A third great fact, partly included in the foregoing statements, is the affinity of the productions of the same continent or sea, though the species themselves are distinct at different points and stations.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XI, “Geographical Distribution”; section “Affinity of the productions of the same continent”. Scope: species assemblages within continents and seas

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch11-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geography-versus-environment contrast is explicit and supported by global distributions and phylogenies. Coverage is broad enough for decisive tests across many clades.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare phylogenetic affinity of species occupying different habitats within a continent or sea against ecologically matched species on other continents or seas. Support requires geography to predict relatedness and replacement better than habitat similarity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Habitat labels require harmonization.

Synthetic phylogenies have uneven resolution.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.96
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Within-region relatedness versus between-region habitat matching is a standard phylogenetic beta-diversity contrast, and both occurrences and a synthetic tree are public. Vertebrates and seed plants are sufficiently covered; many invertebrates are not. Filtering introductions is routine and leaves a decisive comparison for the major regions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare phylogenetic similarity within a continent or sea, across habitats, with similarity between different continents that share a habitat. Habitat matches across continents as close as within-continent relatives would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many branches still lack a complete tree, so some comparisons stay at the level of shared genera.

Recent human introductions blur regional affinity if they are left in the lists.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.85

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Within one continent, the genus-level composition of the fauna/flora of two strongly contrasting habitats (hot desert vs. humid tropical forest) is more similar than the composition of the same habitat type on two different continents; i.e. geographic region, not habitat, is the primary predictor of taxonomic affinity.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: For each of 5 groups (Mammalia, Aves, Squamata, Amphibia, Magnoliopsida) and 10 pre-registered regions (a hot-desert and a humid-forest box on each of 5 continents) the GBIF occurrence API was queried for facet counts of genusKey and familyKey (hasCoordinate, no geospatial issue, PRESENT, 1900-2026, fossil and living specimens excluded). Genera with >= 5 records formed the regional genus set; 11 domestic/commensal genera were removed. Sørensen similarity was computed for all 45 region pairs per group and pairs were classed as within-continent/different-habitat (5 per group), between-continent/same-habitat (20) or between-continent/different-habitat (20). Means were compared per group and a pooled one-sided Mann-Whitney U test (within-continent/different-habitat > between-continent/same-habitat) was run on the 25 vs 100 genus-level pair similarities.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: for each of five taxonomic groups (Mammalia, Aves, Squamata, Amphibia, Magnoliopsida), compute the Sørensen similarity of genus sets (2|A∩B|/(|A|+|B|), GBIF occurrence-derived genus lists, genera with >= 5 records per region) for (i) the 5 within-continent / different-habitat region pairs and (ii) the 20 between-continent / same-habitat region pairs. The claim is SUPPORTED if the mean of (i) exceeds the mean of (ii) in at least 4 of the 5 groups AND a one-sided Mann-Whitney U test pooling all groups' pairs (i) vs (ii) gives p < 0.01.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: REFUTED if the mean of (i) exceeds the mean of (ii) in 2 or fewer of the 5 groups, or if the pooled one-sided Mann-Whitney test in the opposite direction ((ii) > (i)) gives p < 0.05. Any other outcome is MIXED. If fewer than 4 groups have >= 20 genera in every region, the result is inconclusive (underpowered).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: groups (of 5) where within-continent/different-habitat mean genus Sørensen > between-continent/same-habitat mean

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: pooled one-sided Mann-Whitney (within > between-same-habitat), genus level: U=2086, p=1.22e-07

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'productions of the same continent' are taken as the native genera recorded in GBIF within fixed bounding boxes on five continents (South America, Africa, Australia, North America incl. Central America, mainland Asia). 'Different stations' is operationalized as two habitat types with the strongest possible contrast on each continent: a hot desert/semi-desert box and a humid tropical forest box. 'Affinity' is operationalized as sharing genera (and, secondarily, families), which is the pre-phylogenetic measure of relatedness Darwin himself used. The 'same sea' half of the claim is not tested here. Regions are fixed before any data are downloaded; genera of domestic and commensal species that humans have spread worldwide (Homo, Rattus, Mus, Canis, Felis, Bos, Ovis, Capra, Sus, Equus, Columba) are excluded, as are fossil and living (zoo/garden) specimen records, because the claim concerns natural distribution.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: GBIF occurrence search API (facet counts of genusKey/familyKey within bounding boxes; GBIF Backbone Taxonomy for keys)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Magnoliopsida is the one group where the same habitat on another continent is as similar (0.307) as a different habitat on the same continent (0.295); introduced weeds and genuinely cosmopolitan plant genera both contribute, and GBIF cannot flag introductions reliably.

Amphibia is underpowered (as few as 4 genera in the Thar desert box) but the criterion was still met in 4 groups with >= 20 genera everywhere (Mammalia, Aves, Squamata, Magnoliopsida); Amphibia is reported but did not decide the verdict.

Genus sharing is a pre-phylogenetic proxy for 'affinity'; no phylogenetic beta-diversity was computed.

Introduced and vagrant species other than the 11 excluded commensal genera remain in the lists; they bias toward between-continent similarity, i.e. against the claim.

Bounding boxes approximate habitats; each box contains some other habitat. Sampling intensity differs by orders of magnitude between boxes (e.g. Asian desert mammals 2.5k records vs North American desert 237k), which depresses similarity for poorly sampled regions regardless of category.

The 'same sea' half of the claim was not tested.

GBIF is a live resource; re-running reproduces the method but counts drift as records are added. Response checksums at retrieval time are in derived/fetch_log.json.
